name: 40 - The Giant's Den: The Bone Ring

text.content:
STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

The Bone Ring

Optional sixth crime scene. Use if the giant's den is on your finished map, or replace a main murder site. Victim: Odran Pell, an adult gaoler who began counting prisoners the records denied. Culprit: Nella's coven-directed staging. This is not an extra required plot.

The cell passage has been built for hands larger than yours. Iron bars vanish into stone blocks the size of coffins. Beyond them, a table and chair look child-sized, though they were made for ordinary people.

In the open cell, bones have been arranged in a careful ring. Every long bone points toward the next, joint answering joint, until the pattern seems less like a pile of remains than a sentence you have not learned to read.

A broken chair stands in the centre. On its seat rests a cracked helm covered by a pale, stretched mask. The mouth has been left open. A dark thread runs from it to a torn page on the floor.

Someone has set a severed finger on the page like a bookmark. It points at a line with most of the words rubbed away. Only two remain: NAME INTACT.

From somewhere inside the mask comes a breath. It is too late to belong to its owner.

The mask and remains are dead matter moved by a magical tether. They are not evidence that an ordinary corpse has a trapped soul. At a veiled table use a carved mask and a bone pointer; the mystery is unchanged.

Scene truth

Odran discovered that the official prisoner count fell while the occupied cells did not. Nella silenced him and arranged a ritual message. The ring is an inverted mnemonic diagram, intended to isolate a name from recognition. The skin and bones were arranged after death. This replaces the earlier contradictory claim that he was both flayed alive and skinned after death.

pages.name: A solvable scene and the two riddles

text.content:
STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

What the investigators can establish

The cell door has an ordinary functioning lock. It was opened with a key, not broken by a giant. A small incomplete shoeprint appears in ash beside the chair. Three different pressure patterns in the chalk match the three-part pattern from the crystal diagram.

Automatic clues: prison count scratched on the table exceeds the register by five; a pie-delivery slip is folded beneath the register; the hymn page originally concerned preserving the names of the dead. DC 14 Investigation: the bones were arranged after the chair broke. DC 15 Medicine: the ritual arrangement is postmortem. DC 15 Religion: the funerary text has been altered, not faithfully performed.

Speak with Dead

If the party provides access to Odran's remaining intact mouth, the spell works according to its normal requirements. The mask itself is not automatically a valid corpse. Who visited? 'Granny. She brought something for every occupied cell.' What did you find? 'Five more voices than names.' Who had a key? 'She gave it back before I knew she had it.' Where is the proof? 'Under the count book.' What did she say? 'A prison is easier to keep when nobody is missing.'

The mask's riddles

The following are new, cleaner versions of the two requested answer-riddles, retaining the answers UNICORN and BLOOD. The original phrasing is preserved in @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.gm-journals.JournalEntry.a45d4f574d4d78a0.JournalEntryPage.f651ae5028ea95f6]{the archive}. Give @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.handouts.JournalEntry.66a58efdddf8a7b6]{the first} and @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.handouts.JournalEntry.5f4792a87634298a]{the second} separately.

'One spear upon a brow of white, Four hooves that flee the hunter's sight. No soldier I, though crowned for war; What woodland wonder bears no more?'

Answer: Unicorn. Accept the intended answer without debating literal zoology. A carved single-horned horse beside the ring provides a visual hint.

'No mouth have I, yet wounds let me speak. I run when the body's walls grow weak. Within you, hidden; spilled, bright red. What keeps the living from the dead?'

Answer: Blood. The cracked helm bears a painted red drop as a hint.

Speak each answer or turn the matching carved symbol. Both release the black thread from the hymn page and reveal a route sketch to the well. No actual blood, animal harm or self-injury is required. A relevant dispelling effect, examination of the mechanism or removal of the ring's central pin also reveals the clue.

Failure causes the mask to repeat the riddle in a familiar voice; no damage and no permanent lockout.

text.content:

Existing scene artwork

This is the circle-of-bones illustration, held back for reveal after the party enters the cell. Its skull, broken chair, ring of bones and written scrap are illustrative; the exact count of drawn bones is not a coded solution.

The riddle answers are supplied by the written handouts, not by trying to read the image's decorative writing.
